name: super-el-nino-simulator
description: Super El Nino Global Impact Simulator - an interactive R3F globe with a client-side DuckDB-WASM analytics engine.

scripts.dev:all: concurrently -k -n vite,worker -c cyan,yellow "pnpm dev" "pnpm run dev:worker"
scripts.//e2e: Batched: ONE Playwright process per spec file, each with its own server port. The full suite is recorded crashing the browser worker (0xC0000142) part-way through one long serial run under SwiftShader; splitting per file sidesteps it. Retries once ONLY on a worker crash. For a targeted subset use `e2e:raw`, e.g. `pnpm e2e:raw -- --grep globe`; PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never keeps CI from blocking on the report.
scripts.//e2e:raw: Single Playwright process over whichever specs the arguments select. The old `pnpm e2e` behaviour, kept for --grep runs against one feature area.
scripts.//build:e2e: Node wrapper, not `VITE_E2E=1 vite build`: pnpm runs scripts through cmd.exe on Windows, where that POSIX assignment is parsed as a command name and fails, so the E2E bundle was never actually built there.
scripts.//build-stamp: Written LAST in the build:e2e chain so a failed link never leaves a stamp claiming a fresh bundle. tests/e2e/global-setup.ts recomputes srcHash and fails 'STALE E2E BUNDLE' on mismatch — a failed lint/tsc used to leave the previous bundle in place and specs silently measured it.
scripts.//build:e2e-outdir: The E2E bundle goes to dist-e2e/, NOT dist/. Sharing one directory with pnpm build meant the gate replaced the instrumented bundle with a production one and the stamp guard then rejected the next spec run. scripts/build-e2e.mjs forces --outDir, check-assets is pointed at the same directory, and playwright.config.ts serves it.
scripts.build:e2e: node scripts/copy-duckdb.mjs && tsc -b && node scripts/build-e2e.mjs && node scripts/check-assets.mjs --allow-e2e --dir dist-e2e && node scripts/write-build-stamp.mjs
scripts.//e2e:look: Look acceptance suite: the look specs (3.1-3.9 incl. the negative tests) plus globe.spec.ts's five zoom cases. CHAINS build:e2e because the served bundle is dist-e2e/ and a run against a missing or stale bundle is a stamp error, not a measurement — the caller should never have to remember two commands. cross-env because pnpm runs scripts through cmd.exe on Windows, where a bare VAR=val prefix is parsed as a command name.
scripts.e2e:look: pnpm build:e2e && cross-env PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never playwright test tests/e2e/look.spec.ts tests/e2e/negative.spec.ts tests/e2e/globe.spec.ts
